title: Pediatric bone accrual predicted effector genes (Cousminer DL et al. 2021)
bodyHtml:
This table displays results from the study:

Genome-wide association study implicates novel loci and reveals candidate effector genes for longitudinal pediatric bone accrual.
Cousminer DL, et al.
Genome Biol. 2021 Jan 4;22(1):1. doi: 10.1186/s13059-020-02207-9.
PMID: 33397451

The authors performed longitudinal modeling of bone accrual in a pediatric cohort, followed by GWAS for 3 bone accrual parameters measured at 6 skeletal sites. To prioritize potential effector genes, they considered all genes within the topological associated domains (TADs) surrounding all genome-wide significant signals and some suggestive signals (where p-values were less significant but variants were associated with multiple relevant phenotypes). The table below lists the single gene at each locus identified as the most likely effector gene, along with the supporting evidence. Mouse over the column headers for more details about each evidence type.
